pc.name: Point clouds
pc.privacy: The file and the cloud never leave this computer. The file is read here and the tiles are kept in this browser's own storage; nothing is uploaded.
pc.numbers: Everything this tab reports is a number from your data, not a certificate. The registered professional decides what it is good for.
pc.stopped: Stopped. A build keeps what it finished; press Resume to carry on.
pc.info.short: A build needs about {need} but this browser can store {free}. Free some space or use a smaller file.
pc.progress.residuals: Comparing the points with the ground
pc.where.browser: Kept in this browser's own storage.
pc.where.hint: A big cloud takes about as much room as its file. Choose a folder with space, for example a CadCraft clouds folder in Documents; clouds already built stay where they were built.
pc.where.set: Clouds will be kept in the folder {name}.
pc.where.reset: Clouds will be kept in this browser's storage.
pc.o.what: Drape the drone's orthomosaic on the ground and the plan. It becomes a map layer of the project (a GeoTIFF, or a PNG or JPEG with its world file), so the plan shows it under the drawing and the 3D view paints it on the ground you built. Build the ground first.
pc.o.file.hint: Choose the picture together with its world file (and .prj) when it has them. A very large picture is reduced to 16 megapixels.
pc.o.reading: Reading the picture. When the program asks where its coordinates are, answer it: the project's own system, or pick one (a .prj file chosen with the picture answers it for you).
pc.o.none: No picture was added. The message above the drawing says why.
pc.o.added.nocloud: {name} was added as a map layer. Open a cloud to check it lies over it.
pc.o.nocrs: The file has no coordinate system, so it was placed in the project's own coordinates.
pc.o.nooverlap: {name} does not lie over the cloud. The usual cause is a different coordinate system: remove the layer in Map layers and add it again with its .prj file.
pc.o.show3d: Show it on the ground in 3D
pc.o.on3d: The ground in 3D now shows the picture.
pc.o.needground: Press Build ground: the picture is draped on the ground surface.
pc.list.empty: No clouds yet. Open a file above.
pc.list.resume.hint: Choose the same file again, then press Resume.
pc.remove.title: Remove this cloud?
pc.remove.body: {name} will be removed from this browser's storage. The file you opened is not touched.
pc.plan: Show the cloud in the plan
pc.stats: {drawn} of at most {budget} points drawn · {nodes} tiles shown, {loading} waiting · {mb} MB held
pc.clean.hint: Draw an outline in the plan, or in the 3D view from the top view. In 3D the outline is taken down to a level plane, so it selects a vertical column. The count below is shown before anything changes.
pc.clean.draw.lasso: Press, drag round the points, release. Esc cancels.
pc.clean.draw.box: Press at one corner, drag to the opposite corner, release. Esc cancels.
pc.clean.draw.polygon: Click the corners; double-click or Enter closes. Esc cancels.
pc.act.crop: Crop to this boundary (delete everything outside)
pc.label.crop: Cropped to the boundary ({n} points removed)
pc.big.title: That is more than half the cloud
pc.big.body: This changes {n} points, {pct} % of the cloud. It can be undone. Go on?
pc.log.title: Edits so far (the file itself is never changed)
pc.noise.title: Find noise
pc.noise.what: Marks stray points as low points (class 7) or high noise (class 18). Nothing is deleted unless you tick the box. One undo step.
pc.noise.radius.hint: In the file's units. Points count as neighbours inside this distance.
pc.noise.min.hint: Isolated: a point with fewer neighbours than this is noise.
pc.noise.k.hint: Statistical: the mean distance to this many nearest points.
pc.noise.sd.hint: Statistical: further than the mean plus this many is noise.
pc.noise.remove: Also delete the points it finds
pc.noise.done: Marked {n} points ({low} low, {high} high) in {ms} ms.
pc.g.what: Finds the ground tile by tile (256 m tiles with an overlap), compares every point with it and marks ground (class 2) and low points (class 7). One undo step.
pc.g.cell.hint: Grid size for the lowest-point search, in the file's units.
pc.g.tol.hint: A point this close to the found ground is called ground.
pc.g.slope.hint: Steepest ground slope the filter should follow (rise over run).
pc.g.obj.hint: Buildings wider than this many cells are taken out of the ground.
pc.g.start.file: the classes already in the file
pc.g.label: Ground classification
pc.c.label: Vegetation and building classes
pc.g.done: Ground: {ground} points, low points: {noise}, {tiles} tiles, {ms} ms.
pc.g.seams: {n} tile seams disagree by more than half the tolerance. Look at them before trusting the ground there.
pc.g.seams.none: No tile seam disagrees by more than half the tolerance.
pc.c.done: Low vegetation {low}, medium {mid}, high {high}, buildings {building} ({ms} ms).
pc.s.what: Builds the existing ground from the points called ground, then compares those points with it. The ground is added to the project the way the LAS import adds it (points described GROUND), as one undo step.
pc.s.spacing.hint: Thinning for the ground surface, in the file's units.
pc.s.mode.nearest: Nearest the middle of the cell
pc.s.maxedge.hint: Triangles with a longer edge are left out, for example over water.
pc.s.done: Used {kept} of {seen} ground points; {points} points added to the project, {tris} triangles.
pc.s.capped: The point cap was reached; some ground points were left out.
pc.r.honest: These are numbers for this cloud and this ground. They are not a certificate of anything.
pc.r.worst: The ten places that differ most (click to fly there)
pc.bl.title: Breaklines
pc.bl.pick: Pick a breakline on the cloud
pc.bl.hint: Click points along the kerb, ditch or top of bank in the 3D view. Each click takes the nearest drawn point.
pc.bl.plan: Pick a breakline in the plan
pc.bl.planhint: Click along the kerb, ditch or top of bank in the plan. Double-click or Enter ends the line, Esc cancels. Each click takes the nearest cloud point, ground first.
pc.bl.planfew: Fewer than two clicks found a cloud point. Click closer to the points, or zoom in.
pc.bl.plansaved: Breakline kept with {n} points ({skipped} clicks had no cloud point near). The next Build ground uses it.
pc.c.preview: Contour lines over the cloud, seen from above
pc.bl.saved: Breakline kept; the next Build ground uses it.
pc.c.none: No contours yet. Build the ground first.
pc.v.title: Stockpile volume
pc.v.what: The volume of the surface above a base inside a boundary you draw. The boundary should surround the pile on the ground.
pc.v.draw: Click the corners round the pile; double-click or Enter closes.
pc.v.base.quadric: Smooth curved base through the boundary
pc.v.leaves: The boundary leaves the data: {area} square units have no surface and are not counted.
pc.f.title: Volume between two flights
pc.f.what: Builds the ground of {a} and of the other cloud and compares them. Fill is where the other flight is higher, cut where it is lower.
pc.f.none: Build a second cloud first. It appears in the list here.
pc.x.title: Export a cleaned LAS or LAZ file
pc.x.what: Writes the cloud with your edits and classes applied as a new file. The original file is not changed.
pc.x.laz.what: LAZ is LAS compressed without loss: every point comes back exactly. It is written as point format 0, or 2 with colour, in a LAS 1.4 file, by CadCraft's own compressor.
pc.x.all: All points that are not deleted
pc.x.done.file: Saved {n} points ({size}) to the file you chose, written as it went.
pc.x.stream: You choose the file first; the points are then written to it as they are read, so a very large cloud does not have to fit in memory.
pc.x.big: This browser cannot write a file as it goes, so the whole export (about {size}) is gathered in memory first. Use Chrome, Edge or the Studio app for a cloud this large, or export only a region or only the ground.
pc.x.ratio: The file is {pct} % of the same points as LAS.
pc.sec.what: Draw a line across a ditch, kerb or slope: the points within half the width of it are drawn against distance and height.
pc.sec.draw: Click the start, then the end of the line.
pc.sec.out: {n} points, line {len} long, strip {w} wide, heights {z0} to {z1}.
pc.sec.tin: The blue line is the ground you built.
pc.err.no_cloud: That cloud is not in this browser's storage.
pc.err.bad_cloud: That cloud's files are damaged or from another version.
pc.err.building: That cloud was not finished. Choose the file again and press Resume.
pc.err.missing_node: A tile of the cloud is missing from storage.
pc.err.no_opfs: This browser has no storage the add-on can use.
pc.err.bad_source: That file is not a LAS or LAZ file this add-on can read.
pc.err.too_few_points: There are too few ground points to make a surface. Find the ground first.
pc.err.no_surface: No surface could be made from those points.
pc.err.no_ground: This needs the ground found first.
pc.err.resume_mismatch: That is not the same file as the one the build started with.
pc.err.too_many_cells: That asks for too many cells. Use a larger cell size.
pc.err.boundary_off_data: The boundary is outside the data.
pc.err.no_overlap: The two grounds do not overlap.
pc.err.not_configured: The add-on is not set up correctly.
pc.err.bad_params: One of the settings is not usable.
pc.err.laz_class_range: A point has a class above 31, which LAZ point formats 0 and 2 cannot hold. Export it as LAS 1.4, or change that class first.
pc.err.bad_format: That point format cannot be written.
